author: @lreez977
text:
I get why it’s hard for y’all to appreciate Dot. It’s cuz y’all are usually looking for set-ups and punchlines or double entendres like battle rappers similar in the way Drake does them. Which is fine, but Dot writes differently than Drake. Dot writes more like a songwriter so it helps to look for themes and metaphors.

For example, even starting off the track with “I see dead people” is a multiple entendre and a call back to Euphoria. (Dead because he killed them after MTG, Dead because of the 6th sense reference from the AI/6th sense bar/Dead because album art is looking at a vantage point of sex offenders gathering at the Embassy)

Y’all missed so much prior to the A-minor (Stockton, Teezo touchdown, Dee-bo).

Also, with the A-minor bar it’s also a call-back and rebuttal to Drake’s Family Affairs where he stretches “Dave Freeeeeeeeee”.

You also missed the Malibu most wanted extended metaphor.

Y’all evaluate Dot from the lens of battle rap which is why it’s hard for y’all to appreciate him. It’s also why y’all didn’t appreciate MTG. Moreover, it’s why there’s a disconnect between y’all, other Drake fans, and Dot fans.

You have to look at his raps more so through a songwriter lens to fully appreciate them. It’s just different styles. 9:24

author: @DanteKobayashi_
text:
It’s makes me sad to see y’all miss on this entire beef when it comes to the Kendrick side of things. You’re entitled to your own opinions but, you all tend to contradict yourselves every time you make a point of criticism so, to us as viewers it just comes off as either blatant hate or bias towards Drake. 

Claiming it’s a “drought” and asking for more “double entendres” yet, saying that he needs to spell out the bar for you doesn’t make any sense. The A-Minor bar for example wasn’t even the first double entendre you hear in the song lol. (which btw, it’s actually a triple entendre; A Minor is the only scale in music that uses no BLACK keys. Kendrick has consistently talked about Drakes need to “feel” or be “black” so, he’s double dissing him there) I don’t know if y’all just don’t know the full situation/sides for both parties involved in the beef so it was harder for y’all to pick up on some of the initial bars but, you missed so much in this song. 

This song is bigger than just shots/allegations about Drakes pedophile claims. He’s literally standing up for the West Coast image and his roots! He’s essentially telling Drake that he has NO identity in the rap game with his sound. All these different rappers are constantly giving him credibility and falsifying this personality that he now calls “Drake” or “Drizzy.” He consistently steals from other sounds to create his music while never garnishing his own personal sound. (i.e Chicago style, Detroit, West Coast etc) It’s the whole reason the West Coast essentially plays this shit likes it’s their ANTHEM because Kendrick is one of this generations leaders in the West Coast sound and when you are able to have VALUE and IDENTITY within a culture/group of individuals you evolve into something more than just an artist. Drake has NEVER had that his entire career.

I can’t stand Drake, but, when he dropped Family Matters I had to respect that he went off like crazy and it looked like he took a lead in the beef but, Kendrick literally went nuclear on this song and it’s so disappointing as a fan of you guys from the OG Logic mixtape days to see y’all’s takes on this be so horrible and bias.

TLDR - I’m disappointed because I’m an OG of this channel and I feel like you guys missed EVERY part of this song and every other Kendrick song and constantly under appreciate him.

author: @jazzyjakeen9469
text:
As someone who used to follow this channel, I'm disappointed. It is no longer unbiased and definitely cannot be about bars. There are bars - double, triple, quadruple entendres - all throughout every single track he's dropped during this, his flows are all sliding, the character assassination on Drake from an identity, personality, desire standpoint, how y'all allow Drake to present himself as something we know he is not because we've seen with our own eyes where he came from/how he came up to now, and how he does not value those who is supposed to love like his parents, child(ren), mentors, friends, himself. 

Anyone who knows anything about lyricism and rap can say without hesitation that Kendrick is a better rapper than Drake. Can Drake flow on a beat, have good production, the backing for visuals and to push his work? Absolutely. Is he an actual part of the culture, does he switch flows and styles to fit in, does he rely heavily on others to write for him and give him a persona and swag? Absolutely. None of Drake's disses were better than Kendrick's. Taylor Made was trash and disrespectful, coming from someone on the west coast - Family Matters was the best of the bunch but still was elementary when it comes to lyrics. Drake a better battle rapper is comical at best. You playing Drake's clip saying they were all hard hitting is a blatant lie, he is just flowing well and not saying anything scathing. A size 7 man's on hits hard? Come on guys. Drake is a plant and makes music for the masses to be lost in average. 

6:16 in LA was probably the lightest of them all from Kendrick, with the most layered meaning for the title alone. There was no universe where Drake was going to out-rap or have better lyrics than an award winning writer. Is there all kinds of video and photographed evidence of Drake acting strange towards young teenage girls? Yes. If you choose to ignore that then say that. To say you care about these types of allegations then say the only hard hitting lines don't include those bars is crazy. There is a lot more of this within these industries than any of you acknowledge, and it is the biggest thing we should be focused on. Between the allegations, Drake as a man, as a father, as a rapper there is a lot more meat to the diss than Drake saying he's short and allegedly hit his woman (less proof of that than of Drake being inappropriate with minors). To say Drake has more bars and less filler than Kendrick is insanity. Y'all are known for loving a beat even if the lyrics are mediocre. Perfect example is Like That (without Kendrick). The beat was amazing, Future's lyrics were a joke outside of the chorus
